_comment: The single source of truth for what the Loom installs into an adopting repo (Loom 2.0-rc.7 W4). THREE consumers read this file: adopt.mjs (the idempotent installer), the CI adoption dry-run, and the generated copy table in loom-adopt/SKILL.md (a doc-integrity check fails the build when the table drifts from this manifest). A hand-maintained copy list is what let the adoption guide fall behind the machinery — this file makes that impossible. Sources are relative to this harness dir; destinations are repo-root-relative. kind: file | dir | glob. adopt:'template' marks a *.template.* file whose destination drops the .template; the installer copies it but never fills the ADOPT placeholders — activation is the adopter's, recorded honestly in the adoption report.

entries.seam: The discovery canon (single source — do not fork the text)

Every identifier expanded — discovery gates D1–D9, quality gates Q1–Q5, signals, themes, hypotheses, governance ids. Ships with the harness because the runbooks and templates that link it are installed here too
Pure-Node D1–D9 validator + its tests
Zero-dep branded renderer (HTML + OOXML) + tests
One template per discovery artifact
Brand seam (neutral demo instance)
A second brand proving the seam swap
entries.tier_note: core: zero ADOPT burden, and it is the proof the D7 brand seam swaps — the renderer suite asserts against it

entries.seam: One template per delivery decision artifact (ADR · Solution Direction Record)
The backlog SHAPE the delivery loop and the waist gate read — an example beside where yours goes
entries.tier_note: core: zero ADOPT burden, and the shape is what HG-0007 depends on. The installer still does not ship docs/backlog.yaml — a backlog is your content, not a template — so this is the thing to copy from, and the waist gate names it when it cannot read yours

entries.seam: Guided collaboration-surface forms, GENERATED from the git templates (parity-gated)

Decision-routed floor forms (WS5 · Decision D5.4) — an ADR inbox card and an SDR flow, each mirroring the git template it produces. Write class `decision-routed`: authored here, but the decision only becomes real as a signed envelope a second human merges. Ships DECLARED, NOT ACTIVE — WS5's entry gate has not passed

Floor-only forms (WS3 · D3.3) — write class `lives-on-the-floor`, NEVER frozen. The catalog where personal data actually turns up, because it is where people write prose about people: each form carries its write-class banner and asks for roles rather than names, and scripts/floor-only-check.mjs refuses one that has crossed into discovery/runs/
Every gate + its tests (globbed — a per-file list silently drops new gates)
Policy compiler, gate runner, attestations, compiled-requirements (control plane)
Profiles as data: base + jurisdiction + product-type
Pre-write guardrail hooks (pii-guard, spec/test tripwires, shariah-term-guard)

The PII shapes pii-guard.sh reads — mounted data, not code: a new jurisdiction is a row here, never an edit to a security-critical shell script. NOT OPTIONAL and not tierable: the glob above copies only *.sh, and a guard that cannot load its patterns DENIES every write. It ships wherever the hook ships

The declared Islamic customer-facing prose surfaces shariah-term-guard.sh is scoped to. Core because it ships beside the hook it scopes, and it carries NO entries: with an empty list the guard is a no-op, which is the correct and permanent state for a conventional adopter
Hook wiring for Claude Code (merged, never overwritten — a pre-existing settings.json is preserved and a .loom.json sidecar is dropped to merge by hand)
Eight adoption runbooks + the supervised-pilot playbook
How to activate branch protection, IAM, the routine lane
Reference routine auto-merge controller — separated bot identity, gated on routine-qualified + config-reconciliation (rc.12 WS2.3)
entries.tier_note: core because the control catalog cites it as ROUTINE-CONTROLLER.doc_ref, and the catalog may not cite a ghost

entries.seam: The control-plane ownership map (replace @your-org/… — the gate fails until you do)
The machine-readable control state of record
The identity registry (approvals resolve against it)
Allowed-issuers registry for ed25519 attestations
Identity-provider material for human approval assertions (kept separate from service keys)
The P6 join: surface person id → IdP subject → registry identity. Second-line owned; never written by a service
The observer's signed observation that the map is still current (observed, not declared)
Model inventory (pinned, tiered, evaluated, runtime-governed; optional per-domain validation signatures)
Data classification, retention, erasure, residency
The Run→Discovery feedback log
Operational readiness R1–R6 (per service; unparseable ADOPT dates fail until you exercise the drills)
The promotion ladder (rc.39) — one entry per environment: purpose, data classification, who may promote INTO it, what it promotes FROM. Replaces three unmountable ADOPT comments in the release skill
The exposure register (rc.39) — flags default OFF, belong to a governed change, name an owner and a kill path, and expire. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the exposure_control capability
Product-outcome evals (discovery-linked, measures scored, commit-bound)
The second-line-owned routine-change envelope (HG-0013)
The approved control-plane configuration reconciled against live observations (rc.12 WS2.4)
Service-level expectations for continuous-assurance cases (rc.14 WS6)
Approval service-level EXPECTATIONS (rc.37) — read by scripts/approval-status.mjs, which flags a breach and gates nothing
Exception-register policy (rc.37) — the concentration limit, which may be tightened below the shipped floor of 3 and never raised above it

Per-evidence-type retention — how long each sealed evidence type is kept and why. GOVERNED rather than full because twelve of its fourteen types are the ordinary release bundle (provenance, reviews, tests, SAST, SBOM, evals) and a sealed bundle with no stated retention is a gap for any institution, Islamic or not. The harness records the policy; `immutable_archive: true` is a claim about the institution's WORM store that no gate here can confirm. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the evidence_retention capability
Token-spend ledger (a report, never a merge gate)

The SR-* decision register — the record every Islamic structure and change cites. Agents may cite a ruling by id and may never author, alter or approve one; scholars decide Shari'ah. FULL, not core or governed: an institution running no Islamic product should never be handed ADOPT markers for a committee it does not have. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the shariah_governance capability, silent otherwise

WHERE this institution's Islamic data contracts, fixtures and customer copy live — the declaration the product-substance gate reads. It ships DECLARING NOTHING and that is deliberate: the harness cannot tell an Islamic fixture tree from a conventional one, so a template that guessed a path would either scan the wrong tree or fail a bank with no Islamic product. Declaring a surface is the institution's act. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the shariah_governance capability — without this entry the gate would fail an adopter with nothing to copy, which is the defect it exists to prevent

Who holds the Shari'ah committee seats and under what appointment — the composition register scripts/shariah-governance-check.mjs reads. It checks that a cited approver held a seat on the date they approved; it decides no Shari'ah question. Full tier for the same reason as the rulings register

The deposit-side register for investment accountholders — one row per distribution run, each PER/IRR reserve movement carrying its own committee approval. Mount here or split into docs/governance/profit-distribution/<run-id>.json; the gate reads both. The harness reads the RECORD of a run: it cannot recompute an allocation or tell an approved smoothing from a managed one. Full tier — this is the most Islamic-specific file in the bundle

The record of a declared supervised pilot — stage, caps, supervisor, rollback drill, and which adversarial rows from the playbook have been exercised. CORE, because the playbook it belongs to is core and now points at it; a core adopter who reads the playbook must find the file it names. Costs nothing until used: the gate arms on `status: active`, not on the file's presence, so an untouched copy is silent forever. THE HARNESS RUNS NO PILOT AND OBSERVES NO PRODUCTION — it reads the record, and SUPERVISED-PILOT stays Absent until a pilot has actually run

The protected-attribute register and the disparity measurements taken against it. GOVERNED, not full: the join partners (model-manifest.json, identities.json) are both core, and a model deciding about people is not a specialist product the way an Islamic facility is. THE HARNESS MEASURES NOTHING — every number is the adopter's rig, read as a declaration. What the gate holds that a filled-in slot cannot: the measurement is bound to the model pin that ships, so a retrain invalidates its own evidence. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the fairness_evaluation capability (ai-decision-system, from medium), silent otherwise

Where a person is told why, how they challenge it, and the human who can overturn it — the join the `explainability-and-contestability` PA2 section never had, since a plan could satisfy that section in prose while a model shipped the prose never mentioned. GOVERNED for the same reason as the fairness register beside it. Nothing here generates a reason, judges whether one is intelligible, or routes a contest; the gate reports that limit on every run. Mandatory once a compiled plan requires the decision_contestability capability, silent otherwise

Pinned external rule bases — publisher, edition, who owns re-verification, and the bound after which `last_verified` stops counting. The MECHANISM is generic, but three of the four shipped rows are Shari'ah rule bases and `knowledge_currency` only compiles from an Islamic or institution profile, so it sits at full rather than taxing every governed adopter. No gate here ever fetches a publisher: a fresh pin means somebody looked recently, never that the pin is current

The internal Shari'ah audit charter — scope, independence, reporting line and cycle for the third-line review of the Islamic control set. A charter is a DECLARATION the harness stores and links; whether the function is independent in practice is not visible from a checkout and is not claimed. Full tier, with the rest of the Islamic seam
The neutral adapter contract
The provider catalog — roles and the alternatives that fill them. A catalog is an offer: nothing here is mounted until the institution selects it
Which provider this institution chose per role (the choice is recorded, never defaulted)
Runtime-neutral guardrail policy + generated capability matrix (rc.13 WS4 — the Loom never implies coverage a runtime lacks)
BrainKit manifest — identity, version, lifecycle, owners, digests, approvals (draft until owners approve)
BrainKit institutional identity + design language (the D7 projection source)
BrainKit binding vocabulary
BrainKit architecture principles and constraints
BrainKit technology policy (allowed / consult / forbidden)
BrainKit decision rights
BrainKit approved source register (every section grounds in it)
Canonical read-the-BrainKit fragment — referenced from AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, never overwriting them
The reference CI workflow that runs every gate

_tiers: Adoption tiers (adopt.mjs --tier). core = the warp: all machinery plus the governance data whose gate FAILS CLOSED when it is absent, so a core adoption is safe rather than merely small. governed = the product-governance plane. full = estate, floor and institution. MACHINERY IS ALWAYS INSTALLED at every tier — only what an adopter must FILL IN is tiered, because the burden was never the gates (a gate whose input is absent is silent) but the ADOPT markers. Which entries may be deferred was determined by TEST, not by taste: every deferred entry was removed from a real adoption and its gates confirmed silent.
